summary.headline: HFCL Q1 FY27 revenue rose to Rs 1,914.98 crore (up ~120% YoY) with EBITDA margin of 23.25%; order book at ~Rs 26,665 crore and FY27 growth guidance raised to 40%+.
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue, EBITDA and PAT for Q1 FY27, with consolidated revenue of Rs 1,914.98 crore versus Rs 871.02 crore a year earlier and Rs 1,824.12 crore in Q4 FY26. EBITDA margin reached 23.25% against 18.47% in Q4 FY26, and PAT of Rs 245.64 crore compared with a loss of Rs 29.30 crore in Q1 FY26. Management raised FY27 revenue growth aspiration from about 20% to 40%+, and said the margin will not decline this year barring geopolitical shocks. Capex, a Rs 215 crore data-centre connectivity investment, a Rs 580 crore preform plant and a restructuring review with E&Y as adviser were also disclosed.

segments.name: Telecom products (optical fibre, cables, connectivity)
segments.commentary: Contributed 85% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Management said margins of about 30% in telecom have been sustained over the last three quarters, driven by long-term contracts. Data-centre connectivity started this year, with about Rs 100 crore revenue in Q1 and about Rs 800 crore targeted for FY27 against orders of about Rs 850 crore plus.

segments.name: Defence & Aerospace
segments.commentary: FY27 revenue aspiration of about Rs 500 crore, including the proposed aerostructure acquisition expected to complete within calendar 2026. Order book is about Rs 300 crore excluding the acquisition, about Rs 2,300 crore including it. Long-term aim of Rs 3,000 crore+ in FY28-29 and Rs 5,000 crore in the following year.

segments.name: EPC / Army network
segments.commentary: Still loss-making due to Army warranty-period support without billing. Management expects a contract signing in Q2 FY27, mid-Q2 expected, that would cut revenue losses significantly. Full-year profitability not guaranteed.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth raised to 40% and above from about 20% earlier, with management saying it is not based on a single order.
EBITDA margin expected to stay around 23% (not decline) through the year, with no seasonality, barring geopolitical disruptions such as a Suez Canal closure.
Q2 revenue expected to be roughly flat to Q1 (within 5-10%), with no sequential decline in profitability expected.
Total capex of about Rs 640 crore in FY27 and about Rs 615 crore in FY28, including preform, optical fibre and cable expansion, data-centre and defence capex.
Export mix expected at about 60-65% of revenue, with domestic at about 35-40%.
Telecom-adjacent products (unlicensed-band radio, routers, Wi-Fi) expected at Rs 500-600 crore for FY27, margins about 12-15% EBITDA.
capex_capacity: Optical fibre capacity to rise from 28 million fibre km to 34 million fibre km, to be completed by December 2026.
Optical fibre cable capacity to rise from 34 million to 43 million fibre km (management also referenced 45 million km), with data-centre connectivity capacity expanding 5x including subsidiary HTL.
Board approved a greenfield preform plant of 300 MT per annum at Rs 580 crore; location decision expected within the month. Management says in-house preform is at least 30% cheaper than buying.
Board approved an additional Rs 215 crore for data-centre connectivity (miniature multi-fibre and super high-density MPO assemblies); Rs 100 crore to be spent in FY27 and Rs 115 crore in FY28.

Ammunition complex in Andhra Pradesh groundbroken on 15 May 2026. IBR cable capacity above 14 million fibre km across 12 machines, expanding monthly; 14,000-fibre cable under development, 2-3 months away.
demand_pricing: Management expects demand to outstrip capacity for at least 5 years, citing AI, hyperscale data centres and telecom expansion; contracts being signed for up to 10 years.

Indicative export pricing per fibre km: $22-28 for data-centre fibre, telcos lower; overall range $18-28, with prices up significantly in the last six months. Spot prices are 5-15% above 5-year contract rates.

Long-term contracts have annual price reset clauses; management says large raw-material moves would be passed through. Preform cost increases from the start of the next calendar year are expected to be offset by customer price increases and value-added connectivity products.
Management cites 35% US duty on Chinese fibre and US customer reluctance to buy from China as competitive positives.

Order book of about Rs 26,665 crore: about Rs 16,000 crore optical fibre cable; about Rs 22,000 crore expected to execute within 5 years; contract durations range from 3 months to 4 years (cable), with BharatNet at 3 years and O&M at 7 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 guidance conservative given the strong run-rate and tailwinds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prefers to under-promise: guidance moved from 20% to 40%+ growth, and it is 'always good to be conservative'. It did not give a formal annualised figure.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 23% EBITDA margin sustainable, and is there seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the margin comes from average contracts executed through the year, with no seasonality and no single high-margin order. It said the margin can be protected barring geopolitical shocks.

qa_highlights.question: Will preform cost increases hit margins from calendar 2027?
qa_highlights.answer: Some preform contracts run into FY28. Management expects only a few percentage points of pressure, offset by customer price pass-through and higher-margin data-centre connectivity products; overall margin profile is expected to remain the same.

qa_highlights.question: What is the defence order book and what is the acquisition's effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Defence order book is about Rs 300 crore excluding the acquisition, about Rs 2,300 crore including it. Acquisition to complete within calendar 2026; export defence orders about Rs 2,200 crore. BMP-2 modernisation shortlisted, Army trials started 20 May with about 1.5 months to complete.

qa_highlights.question: What is the data-centre connectivity revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 100 crore in Q1 FY27 and about Rs 800 crore for FY27, with orders of about Rs 850 crore in hand. Capacity to rise 5x, with deliveries of cable starting this month and connectivity about a month later.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Army (EPC) contract restore profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the Army contract signing in mid-Q2 FY27, after which EPC revenue would rise and losses fall significantly. It did not commit to breakeven.

qa_highlights.question: How will debt and working capital evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt-equity is about 0.3 and is expected to stay in that range, funded partly by internal accruals. Segment assets rose about Rs 400 crore net of segment liabilities (about Rs 600 crore liability increase).

risks_watch: Geopolitical disruption (e.g., Suez Canal closure) and government contract timing (Army contract signing and trials) could delay revenue and margin recovery.
Preform price increases from the next calendar year, with some older contracts priced below current market, could compress margins if pass-through is incomplete.
Restructuring committee with E&Y evaluating group simplification; outcome and impact on the defence subsidiary (HASPL) structure remain undisclosed.
Management said it is reviewing further fibre capacity expansion, indicating possible additional capex beyond the current plan.
Export concentration (about 60% of revenue) and US hyperscaler dependence; a shift in Chinese competitive pricing could affect realisations.
Q1 included about Rs 300 crore of Q4 unbilled revenue billed in the quarter; watch whether Q2 revenue holds near Rs 1,900 crore.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on demand, margins and growth, with frequent forward-looking claims on pricing and contracts. Evasive on specifics such as pricing details, order-level margins, restructuring outcomes and the Army contract timing, which were described as confidential or still pending.
key_quotes: Based on the progress achieved in the first quarter, healthy order inflows, favourable industry dynamics, expanding global opportunities and improving execution capabilities, we, to the best of our estimates, can raise our aspirations for FY27 to a revenue growth of 40% and above.
I am pleased to share that the Company has achieved EBITDA margin of more than 23.25% in the very first quarter itself.
There's nothing called a particular high-value or high-margin order which we have executed.
So this 23% margin is something minimum we would be able to protect to the best of my information at this point of time out of the orders I have, raw material cost I have.
